title: 2026-11-18_Remaiten_Botnet_Investigation_06c
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a compromised network infected with the Remaiten botnet. This botnet targets Linux-based systems, including routers and IoT devices. Your goal is to identify and analyze the malicious activities, understand the botnet's behavior, and gather evidence for further remediation.
outcomes: Identify suspicious services and their behaviors.
Gather evidence for further analysis and remediation.

levels.title: Suspicious C2 Beacon Service Discovery
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for sending beacon periodically to the C2 Server.
levels.solution:
1. List all services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
This command will list all services, including inactive ones. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names.

2. Check the status of all services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running
```
This command will show you the currently running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or have unusual descriptions.

3. Inspect network connections:
```bash
ss -tunap
```
This command will display all network connections. Look for any connections to external IPs or unusual ports.

4. Identify the suspicious service:
From the list of services, identify the one that is responsible for sending beacons to the C2 server. This service will likely have an unusual name or description.

The hidden flag is a service name.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services and look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the status of all services using `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running` to identify any running services that seem out of place.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Inspect network connections with `ss -tunap` to look for any connections to external IPs or unusual ports.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. Inspect the suspicious service:
```bash
systemctl cat bot-beacon.service
```
This command will show you the configuration of the `bot-beacon.service`. Look for the `ExecStart` line to find the path of the script launched by the service.

2. Examine the beacon script:
```bash
cat /usr/local/lib/.botcache/beacon.sh
```
This script contains the details of the communication with the C2 server. Look for the `c2_port` variable to find the port number.

The hidden flag is a port number.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Examine the beacon script at `/usr/local/lib/.botcache/beacon.sh` to find the `c2_port` variable and determine the port number.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery for C2 Beaconing Service
levels.content: Investigators suspect that the C2 beacon service automatically resumes after the system starts and continues to execute periodically. Determine which system component is responsible for scheduling this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --all
```
This command will list all timers, including inactive ones. Look for any timers associated with the `bot-beacon.service`.

2. Inspect the timer configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat bot-beacon.timer
```
This command will show you the configuration of the `bot-beacon.timer`. Look for the `OnCalendar` line to understand the scheduling.

3. Check the status of the timer:
```bash
systemctl status bot-beacon.timer
```
This command will show you the current status of the timer and its scheduling details.

The hidden flag is a timer name.
